correctness.rationale: For selected cell (i,j), outside degree is exactly n-r_i+m-c_j; domination is equivalent to every row or every column being occupied. The proof bounds omitted rows and columns at low capacities and characterizes equality, then distinguishes each minimum-cardinality regime and derives the occupied-fibre counting polynomial. Cases include all m<n, m=n, capacity ties, saturation and the permutation-matrix intersection. Direct-neighbourhood brute force exhaustively matches each optimum set and count on ten boards across 49 capacity cases. No general claim relies on finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The number of minimum k-limited dominating sets is a natural combinatorial invariant distinct from the already-known optimum size. The exact all-capacity census explains and enumerates two different extremal mechanisms, including a genuine tie where full-column and one-per-column minimizers coexist, and the square-board intersection by permutation matrices. It gives nontrivial explicit multiplicities for arbitrarily large natural rook graphs and parameters.
